title: The future of pocket money
paragraphs: There are many things we remember from our childhood – the games we played, the music we listened to; but what about earning pocket money? This was our first ever wage for completing tasks such as tidying our bedroom or sorting the laundry. Our reward was a handful of coins that we safely stashed away. But now, it seems, parents’ attitude to handing out cash is changing.

There was a time when cash was king – it was the main currency for financial transactions. These days, though, using credit or debit cards, or making contactless payments, are the most convenient ways of paying. So where does that leave handing over pocket money? Research has found that 84% of British parents currently give notes and coins to their children - typically an allowance, including some discretionary spending, of £7 a week.

But banks predict that by 2028 only one in ten transactions will be with cash, and that it's something today’s children will have to deal with. One particular issue is that children may not understand the value of cash because they never see it. Parents face a dilemma too – finding a new way to transfer pocket money, or maybe not bothering to pay it at all.

Giving children lessons about finance at school is important, and the UK’s Money and Pensions Service advises parents to get children started with money as young as possible. Sarah Porretta from the service told the BBC that for parents who no longer carry cash “The trick is to go and get some coins, just so your children have the opportunity to interact with them. Talk about what you are doing with money. If you are paying with a card or with a phone, talk to children about that and link it back to those coins they have handled."

But, of course, many of the goods that young people want to buy – such as add-ons for a computer game – only allow digital transactions. This has led to a number of apps being set up that allow children to track and spend their hard-earned pocket money and parents to transfer money electronically and monitor their child’s spending. Banks also suggest setting up accounts for older children which gives them a cash card to use. But whatever method a parent chooses to adopt, they need to teach their kids that money doesn’t grow on trees!

vocabulary.entry: pocket money /ˈpɒkɪt ˈmʌni/ 零花钱
vocabulary.example: She gets £5 a week pocket money.
vocabulary.translation: 她每周有5英镑零花钱。

vocabulary.entry: wage /weɪdʒ/ n. 工资；报酬
vocabulary.example: The job offers a competitive wage.
vocabulary.translation: 这份工作的薪酬很有竞争力。

vocabulary.entry: sort the laundry /sɔːt ðə ˈlɔːndri/ 分拣衣物
vocabulary.example: I usually sort the laundry into colours and whites.
vocabulary.translation: 我通常会把衣物按彩色和白色分开来洗。

vocabulary.entry: stash away /stæʃ əˈweɪ/ 藏起来；储存
vocabulary.example: She stashed away her savings in a secret drawer.
vocabulary.translation: 她把积蓄藏在一个秘密抽屉里。

vocabulary.entry: hand out /hænd aʊt/ 分发；发放
vocabulary.example: The teacher handed out the exam papers.
vocabulary.translation: 老师分发了试卷。

vocabulary.entry: financial transaction /faɪˈnænʃl trænˈzækʃn/ 金融交易
vocabulary.example: Online banking makes financial transactions more convenient.
vocabulary.translation: 网上银行让金融交易变得更加便捷。

vocabulary.entry: credit card /ˈkredɪt kɑːd/ 信用卡
vocabulary.example: He paid for the meal with his credit card.
vocabulary.translation: 他用信用卡付了餐费。

vocabulary.entry: debit card /ˈdebɪt kɑːd/ 借记卡
vocabulary.example: You can withdraw cash from an ATM with your debit card.
vocabulary.translation: 你可以用借记卡在自动取款机上取现金。

vocabulary.entry: contactless payment /ˈkɒntæktləs ˈpeɪmənt/ 非接触式支付
vocabulary.example: Contactless payment is widely used in supermarkets.
vocabulary.translation: 非接触式支付在超市里被广泛使用。

vocabulary.entry: allowance /əˈlaʊəns/ n. 津贴；零花钱
vocabulary.example: My monthly allowance is just enough to cover my expenses.
vocabulary.translation: 我每月的零花钱刚好够花。

vocabulary.entry: discretionary spending /dɪˈskreʃənəri ˈspendɪŋ/ 可自由支配开支
vocabulary.example: She uses her discretionary spending to buy books.
vocabulary.translation: 她用可自由支配的钱买书。

vocabulary.entry: transaction /trænˈzækʃn/ n. 交易；业务
vocabulary.example: The transaction was completed in five minutes.
vocabulary.translation: 这笔交易五分钟就完成了。

vocabulary.entry: dilemma /dɪˈlemə/ n. 两难境地；困境
vocabulary.example: She was faced with the dilemma of choosing between her career and her family.
vocabulary.translation: 她面临着在事业和家庭之间做出选择的两难境地。

vocabulary.entry: transfer /trænsˈfɜː(r)/ v. 转账；转移
vocabulary.example: I need to transfer some money to my sister's account.
vocabulary.translation: 我需要给我妹妹的账户转些钱。

vocabulary.entry: finance /ˈfaɪnæns/ n. 金融；财务
vocabulary.example: He is studying finance at university.
vocabulary.translation: 他正在大学里攻读金融专业。

vocabulary.entry: trick /trɪk/ n. 窍门；技巧
vocabulary.example: The trick to making good coffee is to use fresh beans.
vocabulary.translation: 煮出好咖啡的窍门是使用新鲜咖啡豆。

vocabulary.entry: interact with /ˌɪntərˈækt wɪð/ 与……互动；与……交流
vocabulary.example: Children need to interact with other kids to develop social skills.
vocabulary.translation: 孩子需要和其他小朋友互动，才能培养社交能力。

vocabulary.entry: add-on /ˈæd ɒn/ n. 附加内容；附加组件
vocabulary.example: The game has several add-ons that you can buy separately.
vocabulary.translation: 这款游戏有几个可以单独购买的附加内容。

vocabulary.entry: digital transaction /ˈdɪdʒɪtl trænˈzækʃn/ 数字交易
vocabulary.example: Digital transactions have become the norm in modern life.
vocabulary.translation: 数字交易已经成为现代生活的常态。

vocabulary.entry: monitor /ˈmɒnɪtə(r)/ v. 监控；监测
vocabulary.example: The system can monitor the temperature of the room.
vocabulary.translation: 这个系统可以监测室内的温度。

vocabulary.entry: cash card /ˈkæʃ kɑːd/ 现金卡
vocabulary.example: You can use a cash card to get money from cash machines.
vocabulary.translation: 你可以用现金卡在自动取款机上取钱。

vocabulary.entry: money doesn’t grow on trees /ˈmʌni ˈdʌznt ɡrəʊ ɒn triːz/ 钱不是从天上掉下来的（意指钱来之不易）
vocabulary.example: You can't buy that expensive toy - money doesn't grow on trees.
vocabulary.translation: 你不能买那个昂贵的玩具——钱可不是从天上掉下来的。

sentences.chinese: 童年有很多值得我们回忆的东西——玩过的游戏、听过的音乐；但赚取零花钱的经历呢？

sentences.chinese: 那是我们完成整理卧室、分拣衣物这类家务所获得的人生中第一份劳动报酬。

sentences.english: Our reward was a handful of coins that we safely stashed away.
sentences.chinese: 我们会把得到的几枚硬币小心翼翼地存起来。

sentences.english: But now, it seems, parents’ attitude to handing out cash is changing.
sentences.chinese: 但如今，父母们给孩子现金零花钱的态度似乎正在发生改变。

sentences.english: There was a time when cash was king – it was the main currency for financial transactions.
sentences.chinese: 曾经有一段时期，现金为王——它是金融交易的主要支付方式。

sentences.english: These days, though, using credit or debit cards, or making contactless payments, are the most convenient ways of paying.
sentences.chinese: 但如今，使用信用卡、借记卡或者非接触式支付，成了最便捷的付款途径。

sentences.english: So where does that leave handing over pocket money?
sentences.chinese: 那么，这对现金零花钱的发放会产生什么影响呢？

sentences.chinese: 研究发现，目前84%的英国家长仍会给孩子纸币和硬币作为零花钱，每周的金额通常为7英镑，其中包含一部分可自由支配的开支。

sentences.english: But banks predict that by 2028 only one in ten transactions will be with cash, and that it's something today’s children will have to deal with.
sentences.chinese: 但银行预测，到2028年，只有十分之一的交易会使用现金，这是如今的孩子们未来必须面对的情况。

sentences.english: One particular issue is that children may not understand the value of cash because they never see it.
sentences.chinese: 一个尤为突出的问题是，孩子们可能会因为从未接触过现金，而无法理解它的价值。

sentences.english: Parents face a dilemma too – finding a new way to transfer pocket money, or maybe not bothering to pay it at all.
sentences.chinese: 家长们也面临着两难境地——要么寻找发放零花钱的新方式，要么干脆不再给孩子零花钱。

sentences.english: Giving children lessons about finance at school is important, and the UK’s Money and Pensions Service advises parents to get children started with money as young as possible.
sentences.chinese: 在学校对孩子进行金融知识启蒙十分重要，英国货币与养老金服务机构建议家长尽早培养孩子的金钱观念。

sentences.english: Sarah Porretta from the service told the BBC that for parents who no longer carry cash “The trick is to go and get some coins, just so your children have the opportunity to interact with them.
sentences.chinese: 该机构的萨拉·波雷塔向英国广播公司表示，对于那些不再随身携带现金的家长来说，“办法就是去兑换一些硬币，让孩子有机会接触它们。

sentences.english: Talk about what you are doing with money. If you are paying with a card or with a phone, talk to children about that and link it back to those coins they have handled."
sentences.chinese: 和孩子聊聊你是如何使用金钱的，如果你用银行卡或手机支付，也要跟孩子解释清楚，并把这种支付方式和他们使用过的硬币联系起来。”

sentences.english: But, of course, many of the goods that young people want to buy – such as add-ons for a computer game – only allow digital transactions.
sentences.chinese: 当然，年轻人想买的很多东西——比如电脑游戏的附加内容——只支持数字支付。

sentences.english: This has led to a number of apps being set up that allow children to track and spend their hard-earned pocket money and parents to transfer money electronically and monitor their child’s spending.
sentences.chinese: 这催生了多款相关应用程序，孩子们可以通过这些应用记录和使用自己辛苦赚来的零花钱，家长则可以通过电子转账的方式发放零花钱，并监控孩子的消费情况。

sentences.english: Banks also suggest setting up accounts for older children which gives them a cash card to use.
sentences.chinese: 银行还建议为年龄稍大的孩子开设账户，为他们办理现金卡。

sentences.english: But whatever method a parent chooses to adopt, they need to teach their kids that money doesn’t grow on trees!
sentences.chinese: 但无论家长选择哪种方式，都需要告诉孩子：钱不是大风刮来的！
